paragraphs: Hyman identifies him as R' Yochanan's student from the formula that, he says, occurs consistently: R' Pernekh said in the name of R' Yochanan, in [Shabbat 14a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.14a.8), [Sukkah 32b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sukkah.32b.4); [Moed Katan 9a](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.9a.8), [Bava Metzia 85a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.85a.18), [Niddah 26a](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.26a.15), and Tanchuma Shelach, Addition 16.
He also reports R' Chanina in [Yerushalmi Pesachim 5:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Pesachim.5.7.2).
At the end of Jerusalem Talmud Sukkah 3:1, the attribution lists Rabbi Chinena, Rabbi Parnach, Rav Matna and Yose bar Menashya, in Rav's name.[^4]

notes.text: The final four-name list does not explicitly mark every transmission link. It is retained without turning all names into independent co-reporters or forcing a sequence.

The saved whole Venice Sukkah 3:1 scalar explicitly has Rabbi Chinena, Rabbi Parnach, Rav Matna and Yose bar Menisha in Rav's name, without intermediate connectors. It supports these exact title occurrences and the list, not a forced chain or four independent reporters. Menisha differs from supplied Menashya; the excerpt does not independently establish END of halakhah 1. Yochanan-student status is Hyman's inference from the repeated reporting formula. The other Bavli, Pesachim and Tanchuma Addition 16 citations were not newly inspected; their title abbreviations remain R'. All source locators and semicolon remain represented.

The five cited Bavli passages and Buber's Tanchuma, Appendix to Shelach 16, contain the Pernekh–Yochanan reporting formula. Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim 5:7 gives Pernekh in Chanina's name in Hebrew; the consulted English spells him “Pamakh.” In the consulted digital Jerusalem Talmud Sukkah 3:1, the names appear in the last paragraph as Chinena, Parnach, Rav Matna and Yose bar Menisha in Rav's name. Hyman's print has Menashya. The text gives no explicit transmission link between each of the four names.

In the linked Bavli passages, Pernekh cites Rabbi Yochanan. Yerushalmi Pesachim has him transmit in Rabbi Chanina’s name. Heilprin records both authorities. Hyman’s Shelach addendum locator is retained as supplied. See [Heilprin’s corresponding entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3013&lang=en).
